claim_classes.established_result: Observed effect or mathematical result within stated assumptions; not unlimited extrapolation.
claim_classes.conditional_model: Prediction conditional on a physical model whose application or empirical status is not settled.
claim_classes.untested_conjecture: Proposed mechanism or interpretation not established by the cited observation.
claim_classes.own_inference: This expedition's comparison, calculation, or proposed follow-up. No novelty priority claimed.

sources.title: Quantum Darwinism in an Everyday Environment: Huge Redundancy in Scattered Photons
sources.authors: C. Jess Riedel and Wojciech H. Zurek
sources.locator: Figure 2(a-b); equations 14-18; isotropic-illumination discussion
sources.supports: Directional illumination makes redundant records. Perfectly isotropic mixed directional states can decohere without redundant records.
sources.limits: Specified scattering model and ideal isotropic limit, not a description of every natural radiation field.
sources.inspection: Read relevant full-text derivation and figures' captions through arXiv HTML.

sources.title: The Rise and Fall of Redundancy in Decoherence and Quantum Darwinism
sources.authors: C. Jess Riedel, Wojciech H. Zurek and Michael Zwolak
sources.locator: Equation 1; sections 3 Pure decoherence and 4 Mixing within the environment
sources.supports: Interactions among environment constituents can redistribute redundant information into collective correlations.
sources.limits: Specific spin models and asymptotic arguments; not every environment scrambles at the same rate.
sources.inspection: Abstract and full-text model discussion.

sources.title: Objectivity (or lack thereof): Comparison between predictions of quantum Darwinism and spectrum broadcast structure
sources.authors: Thao P. Le and Alexandra Olaya-Castro
sources.locator: Abstract and model comparison of mutual information, discord and accessible information
sources.supports: A mutual-information plateau need not consist solely of independently accessible classical information.
sources.limits: Uses explicit model counterexamples. No blanket claim against all quantum Darwinism.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract. The later 2019 equivalence theorem was not relied on because a published comment exists.

sources.title: Perfect Quantum Error Correcting Code
sources.authors: Raymond Laflamme, Cesar Miquel, Juan Pablo Paz and Wojciech Hubert Zurek
sources.locator: Five-qubit encoding and single-qubit error correction construction
sources.supports: Prior work for a perfect five-qubit code protecting a logical qubit against arbitrary single-qubit errors.
sources.limits: Probe uses a standard cyclic stabilizer representation and verifies its properties directly.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract; code representation independently checked numerically in probe.

sources.title: A Theory of Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
sources.authors: Emanuel Knill and Raymond Laflamme
sources.locator: Necessary and sufficient correction conditions, encoded states and recovery
sources.supports: Error correction constrains local operators on the code space.
sources.limits: General framework does not imply natural environments routinely implement a code.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract, together with explicit local-operator checks in probe.

sources.title: Coherence in Spontaneous Radiation Processes
sources.authors: R. H. Dicke
sources.locator: Opening two-emitter example and collective radiation analysis
sources.supports: Collective symmetric and antisymmetric states can have different decay through a common radiation field.
sources.limits: Ideal small-sample and coupling assumptions; real emitters have additional channels.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and primary-paper first-page text.

sources.title: Observation of Superradiant and Subradiant Spontaneous Emission of Two Trapped Ions
sources.authors: R. G. DeVoe and R. G. Brewer
sources.locator: Abstract: distance-dependent spontaneous-emission rate of a two-ion crystal
sources.supports: Measured cooperative emission changes with ion separation.
sources.limits: Does not measure all ideal eta=1 endpoints in this expedition's illustrative model.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract.

sources.title: Inhibited Spontaneous Emission by a Rydberg Atom
sources.authors: Randall G. Hulet, Eric S. Hilfer and Daniel Kleppner
sources.locator: Abstract: conducting-plane mode cutoff; lifetime increase of at least 20
sources.supports: The environment changes an atom's radiative lifetime.
sources.limits: Specific Rydberg transition and geometry; not all decay processes are suppressed.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract verified.

sources.title: Observation of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Atom Spontaneous Emission
sources.authors: P. Goy, J. M. Raimond, M. Gross and S. Haroche
sources.locator: Abstract: resonant superconducting cavity and Rydberg-atom lifetime
sources.supports: A resonant cavity can enhance spontaneous emission.
sources.limits: Specific cavity-transition setting; no general multiplicative factor claimed.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract.

sources.title: Decoherence-Free Subspaces for Quantum Computation
sources.authors: D. A. Lidar, I. L. Chuang and K. B. Whaley
sources.locator: Error generators and protected subspace condition
sources.supports: Protected collective states depend on the noise coupling's algebra and symmetry.
sources.limits: Conditional on the relevant interaction/noise model; extra channels can break protection.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and author-hosted first page.

sources.title: Topological Boundary Modes in Isostatic Lattices
sources.authors: C. L. Kane and T. C. Lubensky
sources.locator: Equation 1; Mechanical Modes and Topological Band Theory; equations 2, 6-7
sources.supports: Mechanical spectra depend on the equilibrium/compatibility matrix; boundary modes can reflect bulk topology.
sources.limits: Spring-framework assumptions. Does not establish topological modes or material constants for the incentre lattice.
sources.inspection: Full relevant arXiv sections and equations.

sources.title: Quantum mechanics and the covariance of physical laws in quantum reference frames
sources.authors: Flaminia Giacomini, Esteban Castro-Ruiz and Caslav Brukner
sources.locator: Results I.1-I.2 and Methods II.5; introduction on invariant probabilities
sources.supports: Quantum-frame transformations alter subsystem descriptions while preserving consistently transformed outcome probabilities.
sources.limits: Formal construction, not evidence selecting an interpretation or erasing operational Bell correlations.
sources.inspection: Full relevant arXiv text; publisher full-text access redirected unsuccessfully.

sources.title: Partial observables
sources.authors: Carlo Rovelli
sources.locator: Sections II-III; https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0110035v2
sources.supports: Distinguishes individual measurable readings from predictive relations among them in covariant physics.
sources.limits: A conceptual/formal framework; does not force a universal ontology of relations.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract and full-text introduction/section structure.

sources.title: Relational Quantum Mechanics
sources.authors: Carlo Rovelli
sources.locator: Original proposal and abstract; all interacting systems treated equivalently
sources.supports: Relational interpretation assigns states/values relative to physical systems without requiring consciousness.
sources.limits: Interpretational proposal. Classification does not claim a distinct falsified prediction; later developments not surveyed exhaustively.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract and opening paper text.

sources.title: Does the missing mass problem signal the breakdown of Newtonian gravity?
sources.authors: Jacob Bekenstein and Mordehai Milgrom
sources.locator: Nonlinear field equation; external-field analysis including equation 32
sources.supports: AQUAL has a uniform external-field effect while preserving universal center-of-mass free fall.
sources.limits: Specific MOND formulation, not verified universal gravity. Linearization in report assumes internal field much smaller than external.
sources.inspection: Primary PDF abstract and indexed equation discussion; report linearization derived directly; external limit cross-checked with R17.

sources.title: Testing the Strong Equivalence Principle: Detection of the External Field Effect in Rotationally Supported Galaxies
sources.authors: Kyu-Hyun Chae, Federico Lelli, Harry Desmond, Stacy S. McGaugh, Pengfei Li and James M. Schombert
sources.locator: SPARC rotation-curve and environmental-field analysis; abstract
sources.supports: Authors report an external-field signal in a MOND-motivated analysis.
sources.limits: Interpretation and significance contested. Report does not repeat detection as established equivalence-principle violation.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract; complementary 2021 analysis abstract also inspected.

sources.title: The phenomenology of the external field effect in cold dark matter models
sources.authors: Aseem Paranjape and Ravi K. Sheth
sources.locator: Sections 2, 3.2.2 and 4; Figure 4; external-limit discussion citing Bekenstein-Milgrom equation 32
sources.supports: Ordinary halo correlations can generate EFE-like statistical signals; mock correlation sign offers a discriminator.
sources.limits: Specific mocks and estimators, not a theorem excluding every MOND or dark-matter account.
sources.inspection: Read full relevant analytical, comparison and conclusion sections.

sources.title: The Modified Dynamics as a Vacuum Effect
sources.authors: Mordehai Milgrom
sources.locator: Sections III-IV; equations 6-11; final distinction between cosmic acceleration scales
sources.supports: A de Sitter detector-temperature difference has MOND-like asymptotics; inertia mechanism remains unspecified.
sources.limits: Special trajectory/background, circular-motion gap and arbitrary choice of response function.
sources.inspection: Full relevant sections and limitations read.

sources.title: Gravitational Decoherence of Dark Matter
sources.authors: Itamar Allali and Mark P. Hertzberg
sources.locator: Abstract: density-superposition scattering by diffuse hydrogen or air
sources.supports: Ordinary matter can gravitationally decohere specified collective dark-matter configurations.
sources.limits: Conditional dark-matter/scattering models; not a detection of dark-matter quantum state.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract checked against repository claim.

sources.title: General Relativistic Decoherence with Applications to Dark Matter Detection
sources.authors: Itamar J. Allali and Mark P. Hertzberg
sources.locator: Abstract: phase versus spatial superpositions in Milky Way axion model
sources.supports: Different collective variables can have very different gravitational decoherence rates.
sources.limits: Specified axion model and environment, not all dark matter.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract checked.

sources.title: Black Holes Decohere Quantum Superpositions
sources.authors: Daine L. Danielson, Gautam Satishchandran and Robert M. Wald
sources.locator: Abstract: soft field excitations carry which-path information into horizon
sources.supports: Horizon degrees of freedom supply a theoretical decoherence channel.
sources.limits: Not an experimental detection or a license for extrapolating rates outside their regime.
sources.inspection: Primary abstract verified.

own_outputs.claim: Identical reduced system states and complete dephasing channels can have different local-record accessibility.
own_outputs.validation: All 32 subsets per construction; commuting conditional states; independent weight-1/2 Pauli check; arbitrary-amplitude dephasing examples.
own_outputs.limits: Finite-dimensional constructed states, not a simulation of generic natural environments.

own_outputs.claim: Equal one-atom marginals coexist with initial two-emitter rates Gamma(1+eta), Gamma(1-eta), Gamma.
own_outputs.validation: Density-matrix evaluation checked against analytic rates for five eta values.
own_outputs.limits: Ideal Markov decay matrix, specified one-excitation states; extra channels excluded.

own_outputs.claim: Extend the Witness Map by separating spreading/decoherence competition, finite-time visibility, and fragment information.
own_outputs.limits: Proposed companion study only; no existing repository changes.

own_outputs.claim: Compare external field strength, gradients, direction and assembly history with matched observation/simulation estimators.
own_outputs.limits: Observational design, no new data or fit.
